title: Chicago white clubs, gangsters and pay
summary: Jones played white nightclubs and theaters, run by gangsters, never colored clubs. He made $150-200 a night and talks about the Haymarket.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Okay. See, I stayed in show business 25 years. I traveled all over the country, that's for sure.
Mainly with these musical acts or dancing?
I played in white night club, played in white theaters, played in the finest places you could find from the show boat in St. Louis on down. Played all over the country.
You play any of the Chicago clubs besides those that you mentioned?
No, I played all these night clubs, but in them days they called them gangsters places. I remember gangsters ran those places. And I played in all them joints.
Dreamland or entertainers? Dreamland was 35th State? Yeah.

No, I never played there. I never played in no colored night club at all. All white. That's right. Over on Lake Street, 63rd and Nairobi, 95th and Western, on Ray Street, so many different night clubs, I couldn't call the name of them.
The white places pay a little better?
Sure, I made $150, $200 a night. Who's that for? I made it as high as $100 a night at the Classic Cabaret. Never touched my salary. That was a worth of thought.
Well, maybe it's worth losing your teeth.
Well, at that time I wasn't dancing right up in here. See, I was on the road. I did Aquabat for a while on the road. Do much theater work?
